component.name: ATK Control
component.summary: Native configuration for ATK/VXE gaming mice

description.p: ATK Control is a native Linux companion for ATK/VXE gaming mice such as the MAD R family and VXE R1. It talks to the mouse directly through its vendor HID collection, so no browser tab, Windows virtual machine or vendor service is required.

Configure the polling rate, up to eight DPI stages with per-stage colours, sensor sampling modes, lift-off distance, debounce, sleep timer, Motion Sync, ripple control, sensor rotation, straight-line correction and the DPI indicator LED. Standard mouse/DPI actions can be remapped per button, and the installed firmware version is shown with a link to ATK HUB for updates. The battery percentage can live in the system tray with three distinctive icon styles, and a small CLI makes the same settings scriptable.
Settings are stored on the mouse itself. The app works offline and sends no telemetry.

description.p: Promotes the ATK Dragonfly A9 Pro Max 2.0 from experimental to verified: its owner tested both links and confirmed that settings are written correctly and survive a power cycle. Lift-off on 0xFF05 mice is a vendor level rather than millimetres, so an unmapped level now reads as "level N (unmapped)" instead of "unknown". The receiver's own firmware is now read and shown for 0xFF05 dongles. The ATK A9 Ultimate sensor is corrected to PAW3950Ultra from ATK HUB's model table, which also fixes every DPI value it read or wrote, which was five times too high.

Adds experimental support for the ATK A9 Ultimate (0xFF02, CID/MID 1,3) over the cable and the 8K dongle, and for the VXE R1 NK NearLink mouse (0xFF05, CID/MID 2,8) over its 1K receiver or cable. Polling, DPI, lift-off, debounce, sleep, Motion Sync, straight-line, ripple, profiles and button remapping are enabled for both; the A9 Ultimate keeps an unmapped lift-off code and an unidentified sensor, and the R1 NK has no lighting, stage colours or rotation hardware. Wired links now report the rate the mouse itself reports instead of a fixed 1 kHz ceiling, 0xFF05 battery replies expose the pack voltage again, and support reports name the configuration protocol. Neither model has been validated on hardware by this project yet.

Adds an experimental, read-only device catalog with twenty-six ATK and VXE identities from the public ATK HUB device list, plus CORE26K sensor support. Recognized catalog models show identity, battery and readable settings but reject writes until their transport is verified. This is recognition, not a claim of full support.

Adds experimental full settings support for the ATK Dragonfly A9 Pro Max 2.0 family over the newer 0xFF05 64-byte protocol: DPI stages and colours, polling, lift-off distance, buttons, lighting, profiles, Motion Sync, ripple, angle snap, debounce and sleep. The protocol was implemented from public reverse engineering; it has not yet been validated on physical A9 hardware, and Bluetooth has no configuration channel.

Adds experimental battery-only support for the ATK Dragonfly A9 Pro Max 2.0 family. The app reads charge level and voltage from the newer 0xFF05 64-byte protocol and keeps every settings page disabled. Also labels these devices as battery-only in scan and support reports.

Adds read-only discovery reports for unrecognised ATK/VXE mice, so a support report can be produced even when the configuration protocol is unknown. Adds `atkctl scan --all`, `atkctl battery` and `atkctl watch`. Hardens button-slot alignment, battery validation, device-picker refresh, tray watcher recovery, hidden error notifications and tray signal caching. Polling writes are now field-scoped to avoid a read-modify-write race.

Adds structured debug logging, retry backoff, profile-commit recovery and safer lock handling; fixes stage-colour canonicalisation and removes the unreachable long-range feature. Adds CLI/transport tests, static-analysis CI, coverage reporting, version-source validation, scoped workflow permissions and pinned actions.

Fixes foreground polling when the window is visible, stage-colour redraws, tray DPI values and IDs, stale charging styling, light-theme drawing, per-stage colour debounce, version derivation and uninstall autostart cleanup. Installs the license file.
Fixes the Flatpak tray bus-name generation introduced by the no-mouse tray visibility change.
Removes the tray item entirely while no mouse is connected, and restores it automatically when a mouse comes back online.
Makes the mutually exclusive tray submenus — polling, DPI, profile and tray icon — use radio items so only the active choice is checked.
Saves settings to the mouse's onboard profile after each change by committing the active profile, so DPI and other values survive a power cycle.
Reduces idle window CPU by only relayouting when displayed state changes, and adds measured performance notes.
Left click now opens the main window, right click opens the tray quick menu, and middle click refreshes.

Fixes the tray context menu's DBusMenu revision and recursive layout encoding, and adds a five-second receiver-only heartbeat so a powered-off mouse is detected without waiting for the hidden-window battery poll.
Adds Angle snapping to the tray quick menu and includes the current DPI value in the tray DPI picker.
Detects when the paired mouse goes offline and automatically switches to the other connected mouse, with a live receiver-online check and faster unplug detection.
Fixes Flatpak tray registration after the unique-name hardening, while keeping the dynamic battery icon and standard menu path.
Fixes the tray icon to use the dynamic battery pixmap and a standard DBusMenu path with a unique item name; adds automatic switching to the other mouse when the selected one is unplugged or asleep.

Safety and trust release: opt-in raw support reports, per-device process locking, recoverable button reset, verified-model gating for remapping and MAX sensor mode, shared-row-safe DPI stage addition, atomic preferences, adaptive tray polling and release checksums.
Shows the paired mouse name separately from the 1K/4K/8K receiver throughout the app and in the window title; clarifies receiver-sleep messages.
Adds button remapping, sensor sampling modes, add/remove DPI stages, live firmware reporting, correct 1/2 mm lift-off handling and a firmware link to ATK HUB.
Rebranded as ATK Control, added the Reticle tray icon and a first-class device support report flow for ATK/VXE mice.
Adds hardware-verified VXE R1 Pro 4K receiver support, including 2,000 and 4,000 Hz polling.
Adds hardware-verified VXE R1 Pro support through its 1K receiver and a receiver picker when multiple devices are connected.
First release with MAD R family support, 8K receiver support, tray integration and CLI.
